name: Griscelli Syndrome Type 3

criteria.description: Presence of partial albinism with silvery-gray hair
Lack of immunodeficiency or hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis features
Absence of mutations in RAB27A gene differentiating from type 2
Identification of mutations in MLPH gene
Hair shaft microscopy showing large irregular clumps of melanin granules

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of partial albinism with silvery-gray hair, absence of immunodeficiency, and confirmed MLPH gene mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires genetic confirmation to distinguish from other Griscelli syndrome types.

laboratory: Normal immune cell counts and function
Hair shaft microscopy showing large melanin clumps
imaging: Occasional mild nonspecific findings if neurological symptoms present
other: Clinical observation of silvery-gray hair and hypopigmentation
Exclusion of immunodeficiency and hemophagocytic syndrome

distinguishingFeatures: Neurological impairment with severe developmental delay
Presence of immunodeficiency absent in type 3

redFlags: Onset of immunodeficiency or hemophagocytic syndrome symptoms
references: Ménasché G, Pastural E, Feldmann J, et al. Mutations in RAB27A cause Griscelli syndrome associated with haemophagocytic syndrome. Nat Genet. 2000.
Ménasché G. Griscelli syndrome: a model system to study vesicular trafficking. Pigment Cell Melanoma Res. 2005.
